reason: The narrative presents the opposite dynamic. The text explicitly condemns Eli, the high priest and leader, for failing to restrain his sons' wickedness. God declares through Samuel that He will judge Eli's house forever specifically because of the leadership's moral failure. The phrase 'בַּעֲוֺן אֲשֶׁר־ יָדַע כִּֽי־ מְקַֽלְלִ֤ים לָהֶם֙ בָּנָ֔יו וְלֹ֥א כִהָ֖ה בָּֽם' (because he knew his sons were cursing/acting wickedly and did not restrain them) directly indicts the leadership. The people's military defeat and loss of the Ark appear to be consequences of this leadership failure rather than the people being 'in the wrong.' Eli dies in shame upon hearing of the disaster, and his family is judged—not vindicated.
